newsitem.title: JAPAN: Wider rupiah band effective for flows - Djiwandono.
newsitem.headline: Wider rupiah band effective for flows - Djiwandono.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Thursday a widening of the rupiah band has been effective in the past in dealing with inflows and outflows of funds, but added he was not sure if this was enough to deal with the current turmoil in Asian currencies.

Donors to Indonesia have expressed concern over what is going on in the Asian region with respect to Indonesia following attacks on the Thai baht, the Malaysian ringgit and the Philippine peso, Djiwandono said.
He said Indonesia explained to the donors what Indonesia has been doing, such as widening the rupiah band.
"This kind of policy step in the past has been effective in facing incoming and outgoing of funds. We don't really know whether that is enough."
He said Asia-Pacific nations have intensified cooperation over the past two years.

The next meeting of Asian central bank governors, in Shanghai later this month, will be a forum to discuss what kind of cooperation can be taken in the face of turbulence in Asian currencies, he said.
Djiwandono said he did not know whether the current steps were enough to cope with turmoil in Asian currencies.
Djiwandono is in Tokyo for a meeting hosted by the World Bank in regard to a loan package for development projects in Indonesia.
